claim: Astrophysics Wrapped 2025 (arXiv:2602.12303, Sec. 2.1) states that 18,660 papers were uploaded to astro-ph in 2025. The count excludes both replacements and cross-submissions, so it covers primary-category papers only.

Table 1 of arXiv:2602.12303 gives the 2025 primary-subject counts: astro-ph.GA 4,761; astro-ph.HE 3,869; astro-ph.SR 2,958; astro-ph.CO 2,789; astro-ph.EP 2,293; astro-ph.IM 1,722; astro-ph (general) 268. Of the 18,660 total, GA plus CO is 7,550 (40.5%) and GA plus CO plus HE is 11,419 (61.2%).

Estimate built on a sourced base and an assumed share: about 1,200 papers on galaxy cluster physics among the 18,660 primary astro-ph papers of 2025 (strict range about 950-1,550, i.e. about 5-8%), and about 2,000-3,000 under a broad definition. The survey's central figure of about 1,500 sits at the top of the strict range, so it is somewhat high but not ruled out.

arXiv:2511.12353 (AstroMLab 5): the dataset covers 408,590 astro-ph papers from 1992 through July 2025. The full text gives no per-year paper totals and no galaxy-cluster, ICM or SZ concept count. The only quoted counts are example ADS keywords (e.g. 'galaxies: evolution' 16,321, 5.5%) and example concepts (e.g. 'Gravitational Lensing Surveys' 278). An all-years cluster share therefore cannot be derived from the paper text; it would need the public GitHub concept CSV.
